We try to follow the rules prescribed in semantic conventions for naming spans. Check our https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.24.0/docs/messaging/messaging-spans.md#span-name perhaps it would make sense to treat this destination as temporary? or maybe anonymous (I think the `MessagingSpanNameExtractor` doesn't implement a special case for it, but shouldn't be hard to add). There is currently ongoing work for implementing the latest messaging semantic conventions (will initially be behind a flag) so also check out https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/messaging/messaging-spans/#span-name there is dedicated settle operation there (I think we have not implemented this yet) and also `messaging.destination.template` that might be useful here (this should be implemented).
cc @trask

replies.body: Addressed in 068f231bc5: JetStream ACK subjects now use a dedicated settle client instrumenter, standard messaging span naming, and messaging.destination.template=$JS.ACK. Normal publishes remain unchanged.

threads.body: This instrumenter is also selected under the old messaging conventions, which have no settle operation, so ACK spans get `messaging.operation=settle`, the name `$JS.ACK settle`, and kind `CLIENT`. RabbitMQ and the AWS SDK gate settle routing on `emitStableMessagingSemconv()`; normalizing the ACK destination under the old publish shape would bound the cardinality without inventing an operation.

`messaging.operation.name` is meant to be the NATS API operation, matching the comment above the other operation-name constants in this file and the settle instrumenters for RabbitMQ (`ack`, `nack`, `reject`) and SQS (`delete`). The published body identifies which one: `+ACK`, `-NAK`, `+WPI`, `+TERM`.

JetStream settlements recorded `messaging.client.operation.duration` while they went through the publish instrumenter, and this one registers no operation metrics.

```suggestion
            .addAttributesExtractor(
                messagingAttributesExtractor(
                    getter, MessagingOperationType.SETTLE, "settle", headers))
            .addOperationMetrics(MessagingConsumerMetrics.getForOperationType());
```

`Message.ackSync()` sends its `$JS.ACK.` settlement through `Connection.request()`, which still picks `requestInstrumenter`, so it keeps the generated subject as the span name and as `messaging.destination.name`. (also in the javaagent `ConnectionRequestInstrumentation`)

`getDestination` feeds `messaging.destination.name`, so this replaces the concrete subject with its template and the span carries the same value under both keys. The stable span name already comes from `getDestinationTemplate`, so the real subject can stay here and the legacy name can be bounded on its own.

Tests import the matching semconv constant instead of building the key by hand.

```suggestion
                                    equalTo(MESSAGING_DESTINATION_TEMPLATE, "$JS.ACK"))),
```

(same at lines 146-147; the `stringKey` import is then unused)

threads.body: [General] The stable-only gate leaves the default V0 messaging mode on the publish/request instrumenter, so its span name still contains the generated `$JS.ACK...` subject. This means the cardinality fix does not apply for users with the default configuration. Route settlement requests to `settleInstrumenter` in both modes and update the old-semconv assertions accordingly.

[General] Settlement wrapping is disabled in the default V0 messaging mode, so `message.ack()`/`nak()` continues without a normalized settlement span for default-configured library users. Enable the wrapper for JetStream messages independently of semconv mode; the settle instrumenter already contains a legacy normalized span-name path.

[General] In the default V0 messaging mode this still chooses `publishInstrumenter`, whose span name includes the complete generated ACK subject. Consequently the reported high-cardinality behavior remains for default javaagent users. Route settlement publishes through `settleInstrumenter` regardless of semconv mode.

[General] This stable-only condition keeps request-based acknowledgements on `requestInstrumenter` under the default V0 messaging configuration, retaining the generated subject in the span name. Select `settleInstrumenter` for JetStream settlement subjects in both semconv modes.

[General] This instruments settlement only for callback-delivered messages. Pull/synchronous consumers receive messages from `Subscription.nextMessage()` (or JetStream pull APIs), and those messages never pass through this handler; because the library wrapper delegates those subscription APIs unchanged, their `ack`/`nak` calls still produce no settlement span. Wrap messages returned by pull subscriptions (or instrument a common message-return path) and add an integration test for that consumption style.
[Style] `AttributesBuilder.put` already ignores a null value, so this guard and forwarding local are redundant. Pass the operation name directly to `put`.

[Testing] This regression only calls `publish`, so it does not exercise the newly added settlement selection in the synchronous and asynchronous request paths (`OpenTelemetryConnection.request*` and `ConnectionRequestInstrumentation`). Those branches can regress independently while this test remains green. Add shared request tests for a `$JS.ACK...` subject (sync and future variants) that assert the normalized legacy span and the stable CLIENT/settle span.

threads.body: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/messaging/#messaging-operation-name give `nack` as a sample. @trask should we try to use a common set of names for common operations or should these be system specific? The attribute description does say `The system-specific name of the messaging operation.`
@trask should we spell this out as `terminate` or is `term` fine?

I think ideally we should use the standard messaging span name extractor. Would it work if for settlement operations we had a custom getter like in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/523c42815293f6e696d8e49d9d8e555438ec617e/instrumentation/redisson/redisson-common-3.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/redisson/common/v3_0/RedissonInstrumenterFactory.java#L25-L32 that overrides the destination name when needed?

replies.body: Looks like currently this won't be enough as `MessagingSpanNameExtractor` takes the operation name as parameter but here the operation name is derived from the request for settle operations. Perhaps the operation name in `MessagingSpanNameExtractor` needs to be changed to `Function<REQUEST, String>`. cc @trask
